To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
during iron overload, the kidney reabsorbs iron through alternative pathways and that iron reabsorption in the kidney is a crucial factor in the regulation of erythropoietic iron usage.

during iron overload, megalin/cubitlin and ferritin are up-regulated and ferroportin is not down-regulated in the kidney, which may enable efficient iron reabsorption and thereby enable the kidney to sense systemic iron.
the route of iron through kidney is regulated during iron overload, and that the renal erythropoeitin producing cells are likely to sense iron overload through iron re-absorption by the kidney.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

iron overload leads to a re-distribution of iron in the kidneys, which is accompanied by a re-distribution in the expression pattern of proteins that are involved in the regulation of iron metabolism.

iron overload in kidney is a complex and dynamic process, with a multitude of iron handling proteins that may play a role, and the exact contribution of each of them may be different under different conditions.
the kidney has an important function in iron metabolism, and the regulation of the kidney iron handling is complex and not yet fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kidney, as a major organ for iron trafficking, plays an important role in systemic iron homeostasis.
the kidney plays an important role in iron trafficking during iron overload and that the regulation of iron trafficking through the kidney is orchestrated to facilitate systemic iron retention.
the kidney, in addition to its role in erythropoiesin regulation, also plays a role in the regulation of systemic iron homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
iron overload is not only a disease of iron storage organs like liver and spleen, but also affects other tissues and organs like the kidney.
the kidney has an important role in the regulation of iron metabolism, which is not only limited to erythropoieses, but also involves the systemic iron state.
